title: Megyn Kelly Tells Olivia Rodrigo to ‘Stick to Singing’ After Speaking Out About Cornell 7 Case: ‘You Don’t Know What the F— You’re Talking About’
description: Following Olivia Rodrigo’s statement in support of the Jane Doe at the center of the Cornell 7 lawsuit on Sunday, Megyn Kelly is firing off at the s
body:
Following Olivia Rodrigo’s statement in support of the Jane Doe at the center of the Cornell 7 lawsuit on Sunday, Megyn Kelly is firing off at the singer, calling her a “know-nothing moron” who should “sit down and be quiet.”

	“Olivia, in sum, you don’t know what the fuck you’re talking about. Shut up and stick to singing,” Kelly said on a Monday episode of her YouTube show. “I liked you better when you were in front of a microphone singing your weird little depressing songs.” She continued: “It’s better to keep your mouth shut and let people suspect you’re an idiot than to open it and prove them right. Ever hear that saying? It applies to you, sweetheart… We don’t need the participation of know-nothing morons who have been auto-tuned into fame and suddenly think they have something profound to say on the culture wars.”
	

	The previous day, Rodrigo had shared a post to her Instagram story writing: “Shame on Cornell and on every institution who protects rapists and abusers over women. I stand with Jane Doe. Her bravery reverberates across the country and the crimes against her will not go unpunished. What she lived through matters, and so does the failure of those who could have intervened but chose not to. She deserves answers, consequences, and lasting change.”


	The Cornell 7 lawsuit refers to the legal document filed by an unnamed Cornell University student who accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and faced no legal consequences. Her lawsuit filed against the university claimed that the school failed to protect her and prevent the alleged assault.
	

	Following an investigation by the university at the time, two of the men were expelled, while the other five received lesser punishment. The lawsuit claims that some of them wrote essays to the school to reduce their disciplinary action, according to her attorney.

	Florence Pugh, Mariska Hargitay, Hudson Williams, Josh Gad and more celebrities have used their platforms to condemn the case in recent weeks.

title: Co-Founder Nate Bolotin to Exit XYZ Films After Almost Two Decades With Studio (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Co-founder Nate Bolotin is leaving XYZ Films after almost two decades with the studio, Variety can reveal exclusively. 

	Bolotin started the label
body:
Co-founder Nate Bolotin is leaving XYZ Films after almost two decades with the studio, Variety can reveal exclusively. 

	Bolotin started the label in 2008 with partners Nick Spicer and Aram Tertzakian. Since its founding, XYZ has grown into a global film studio, encompassing production, financing, international sales and distribution.

	“Nate has been a trusted partner and friend since the company’s inception,” XYZ Films said in a statement. “Our entire team recognizes and appreciates his contributions over the past eighteen years as we’ve grown from a scrappy start-up into the company that we are today. We’re excited to see what he does next.”
	

	XYZ Films continues to be overseen by Spicer, CEO, Maxime Cottray, COO, and Tertzakian, Head of Creative. Key execs include Guy Danella, Head of Film, Pip Ngo, EVP of Sales & Acquisitions, and Marie Garrett, SVP of Sales & Acquisitions.


	Upcoming titles from XYZ include “Flesh of the Gods,” with A24, starring Kristen Stewart and Wagner Moura and directed by Panos Cosmatos; “Egg Baby,” with Amazon MGM Studios, starring Ariana Greenblatt and directed by Natalia Anderson; “Banquet,” starring Meghann Fahy and directed by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia; and “The Girlfriend,” starring Glenn Howerton, Meghann Fahy and Rosario Dawson and directed by Natalie Morales.

	Previous XYZ works include Gareth Evans’ “The Raid” (2012) and “The Raid 2” (2014); Karyn Kusama’s “The Invitation” (2016); Babak Anvari’s “Under the Shadow” (2016); Macon Blair’s “I Don’t Feel at Home in This World Anymore” (2017); Panos Cosmatos’ “Mandy” (2018); Joe “Arctic” (2019); and Matt Johnson’s “BlackBerry” (2023).

title: David Ellison’s ‘Day One’ Skydance Press Conference: Studio Lot Dibs, Trump Ties and Everything Else We Learned
description:
And just like that, David Ellison is in the driver’s seat.

	The newly minted executive leadership team at Skydance, led by chairman and CEO Ellison
body:
And just like that, David Ellison is in the driver’s seat.

	The newly minted executive leadership team at Skydance, led by chairman and CEO Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz, held an on-the-record press gaggle at the Paramount lot in Hollywood, hours after their hard-fought acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed.

	Both in jeans and black blazers, Ellison and Kreiz fielded questions from the national press for nearly 30 minutes on the lot’s Stage 3. The event kicked off with a high-octane trailer showcasing the staggering amount of IP Skydance now owns — from Batman to “Game of Thrones,” the Star Trek universe to “Scream.”
	

	Present for the event were RedBird Capital founder and Skydance board member Gerry Cardinale; Skydance president Andy Gordon; chief legal officer and global president Makan Delrahim; motion picture group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein; chief content officer Casey Bloys; DC Studios co-chair Peter Safran; Skydance CMO Rebecca Mall; DTC exec JB Perrette and many more. Here’s what Variety learned on the ground.

	
		Real Estate	

	Having acquired a jewel like the Warner Bros. lot, along with the historic Paramount spread, questions turned to where, exactly, Ellison and Kreiz will lay their briefcases.

	“We absolutely will keep both lots, and from that standpoint, you’ll probably see us organize film on one, television and streaming on another,” Ellison said. “We’ll go back and forth, as well as to the east coast as required and to our Santa Monica offices for animation.”

	We’d venture to guess that Burbank’s Warner lot, where founder Jack Warner’s rose bushes still bloom, will be the home for feature films. No final decisions, of course, have been made.
	
	
		The Chief Split	

	How will Ellison and Kreiz handle individual duties? The former Mattel CEO addressed their respective workloads.

	“All the business units report to both of us, and there will be natural delineation between us in terms of our respective experience and concentration, which we believe are highly complementary,” said Kreiz. “David will focus on creative technology, long-term strategy — especially as it relates to the creative part of the business. I will focus more on the operations and the day-to-day management of the business, including integration, particularly the first phase. But it’s important to say that we work closely together. It’s not that David will not be very involved in integration and key operational decisions, or that I will not be involved in creative matters.”
	
		The Trump of It All	

	A tense moment came as a reporter grilled Ellison on the company’s ties to President Trump. The journalist referenced an early comment from Ellison that he’d had “great conversations with Donald Trump about CNN.” 

	Pressed for the contents of those talks about the cable news giant he just acquired, Ellison said, “For absolute clarity, we have not talked to any political leader of any party about news, other than to say that we want to be in the truth business and we want to be in the trust business, and we believe in complete editorial independence.” A rep asked the mogul to provide more context on why he’s spent months traveling to D.C.

	“Makan and I started working on a federal [tax incentive for production] in October of last year. Paramount’s domestic production level is about 5%. These jobs are being shipped overseas. Almost no filming happens here in California, which is the birthplace of the business. That’s something we want to change,” Ellison said. “It was the late Senator Lindsey Graham that shepherded that endeavor. We had multiple meetings with the president and Senator Graham, which is really what got the president to effectively say, ‘Yes, I see this, and yes, I want to support this.’ A federal rebate can only get done bipartisan.”
	
		Skydance Film: Producing 30 Movies a Year Will be a Delicate Dance	

	Ellison and Kreiz explained that new motion picture chiefs Goldberg and Greenstein will be responsible for “choreographing” the release schedules for the combined Warner Bros. and Paramount film slate, which boasts 35 movies in its first year. With one movie released every 11 days, and six of those dates overlapping with other titles, how can the studios avoid cannibalizing each other at the box office?
	

	“One of the things we’re not doing is pulling back on creative resources. We’re not pulling back on marketing resources to make sure that we can ensure that all of those films are released properly with the attention that they deserve,” Ellison said. “Dana and Josh will manage the schedule appropriately to make sure that we maximize profitability and maximize the opportunity for every single story we tell.”

	It all comes down to coordination, Kreiz chimed in. “The plan is to keep the studios independent creatively. And then we will choreograph the release schedule to optimize by genre, by audience demographic to achieve the best for the company as a whole.”

	To the point about keeping the studios’ individual identities intact, the Warner Bros. and Paramount logos will be the first audiences see at the beginning of each studio’s respective films — with “A Skydance Company” billed below.

	“When you put the names together, it felt like you were diminishing that legacy,” Ellison said, unpacking their thought process. “We deeply respect and love these brands, and this felt like a way to build something new while honoring the incredible legacy that we are fortunate to be stewards of.”

	Ellison and Kreiz emphasized that they’re equally invested in spending on original films as in leveraging that gargantuan stable of IP.

	“We are going to make a completely diverse slate,” Ellison said, pointing to the success of Warner Bros.’ “Sinners” as an example. (The $90 million blockbuster from filmmaker Ryan Coogler was his favorite movie of 2025, he professed.) “You absolutely will see us tell original stories, continue our franchises, and produce across all genres.”

	Bearing that in mind, when is “Barbie 2” a go? “It’s too early to talk about that,” Kreiz said.
	
		Cord cutting?	

	Skydance has no plans to divest any cable networks or merge its three TV studios — at least not yet.

	Kreiz said the decision to keep Warner Bros. TV, CBS Studios and Paramount TV Studios as separate entities with their own leaders (all reporting to George Cheeks, the newly appointed Skydance TV co-chair and chief content officer) is all “about scale. We’re not looking to reduce output production.”

	Warner Bros. TV boasts more than 80 original series, while CBS Studios produces close to 60 series and Paramount TV Studios has a hefty lineup as well. Kreiz said he didn’t think the studios would compete with each other in the same way they had in going after projects — but at the same time, he added, “to create quality content, that you attract the right talent, that you can actually shepherd these projects properly, you need to keep certain creative parts independent and have them run and operate semi-autonomously. In the sense that the company is still one platform, we will coordinate and align and not compete directly.”
	

	As for the approximately 50 cable networks that Skydance will now operate — combining Warner Bros. Discovery U.S. networks and Paramount’s media networks under Channing Dungey (who reports to Cheeks), Kreiz said keeping that hefty roster was also about achieving “economic scale.” Most of those networks aren’t in the active programming business, but they still secure license fees that are important revenue drivers for the company’s bottom line.

	“The number one priority for the company is to establish Skydance as a content engine, a leading content engine in the world, and this is really the ethos of what this company is about,” Kreiz said. “The investment thesis is about increasing output and establishing the company as a linear content engine. When you do that, you can then drive growth in the digital business. You can continue to optimize your linear channels around the world, which is a large business.”

schema.headline: David Ellison’s ‘Day One’ Skydance Press Conference: Studio Lot Dibs, Trump Ties and Everything Else We Learned

title: Skydance Sets Leadership Across Games, Experiences, Consumer Products and HR
description: Skydance president Andy Gordon has solidified leadership positions across key areas outside the newly merged company’s TV and film divisions, includ
body:
Skydance president Andy Gordon has solidified leadership positions across key areas outside the newly merged company’s TV and film divisions, including games and experiences, products and publishing, HR and global operations.

	Additionally, Skydance has revealed that Paramount and WBD’s games and experiences divisions will be merged into one team which will oversee projects based on IP ranging from Paramount’s “Star Trek,” “Mission: Impossible,” “SpongeBob SquarePants,” “South Park,” “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and “The Godfather” to Warner Bros.’ “Harry Potter,” DC Universe, “Mortal Kombat,” “The Matrix,” “Rick and Morty” and “Game of Thrones.”
	

	Notably, this means combining the newly formed Paramount Games Studio with Warner Bros. Games’ internal video game developers, including Avalanche Software (the makers of “Hogwarts Legacy”), NetherRealm Studios, Rocksteady Studios, TT Games and the WB Games teams in Montreal and Boston.


	In an email sent to staff Tuesday evening, which was obtained by Variety, Gordon announced the following:


Tony Driscoll will be president of games and experiences, in addition to leading corporate strategy and development
Josh Silverman will be president of global products and publishing
Jim Sterner will remain chief people officer and continue to lead HR operations
Jose Turkienicz will continue as president of global operations, including real estate, procurement, and studio operations, with a “focus on simplifying processes and improving service to our businesses so teams can bring ideas to market faster”
Jeff Silberman will be Gordon’s chief of staff in addition to continuing as executive vice president of corporate strategy



	“We’re investing in our future growth engines alongside our core ambitions in TV, Film and direct-to-consumer: Games, Experiences, Consumer Products, and Publishing,” Gordon wrote. “These are core pillars of our strategy to build engagement and fandom in both the physical and digital worlds. We want to meet consumers where they watch, play, and engage. At the same time, we see opportunities to build on DC Comics’ storytelling and expand our e-commerce offerings to connect fans with the brands they love.”

	Games and experiences chief Driscoll (who was named head of Paramount’s newly launched video game studio in June, a combo of Paramount and Skydance’s gaming assets) laid out early plans for his team in his own memo.
	

	“We immerse our guests in theme parks, resorts, restaurants, retail, studio tours and more. We immerse our players in action, adventure, combat, competition and creativity, from ‘Batman’ to ‘SpongeBob,'” Driscoll wrote. “And no matter your role on this team, you are a creator, builder, operator, and steward of those worlds. We have the opportunity to create amazing spaces where friendships are formed and communities grow. That is only possible because of your hard work and talent. Whether it’s on Zoom or in person, my first priority in the coming weeks is meeting as many of you as I can from LA to London, Montreal to Tokyo, and beyond.”

schema.headline: Skydance Sets Leadership Across Games, Experiences, Consumer Products and HR

title: Eddie Redmayne’s Kore-eda Hirokazu Film Is Still Being Scripted, Director Says at Busan
description: Eddie Redmayne‘s upcoming collaboration with Kore-eda Hirokazu is still at the screenplay stage, the Japanese filmmaker said Wednesday at a Busan In
body:
Eddie Redmayne‘s upcoming collaboration with Kore-eda Hirokazu is still at the screenplay stage, the Japanese filmmaker said Wednesday at a Busan International Film Festival press conference for his manga adaptation “Look Back.”

	“Right now, I am writing the script,” Kore-eda said about the Searchlight Pictures film. “I cannot share specific plot details at this stage, but preparations are progressing smoothly. Please look forward to it.”
	

	The director did not disclose a title. He expects to go public formally next year at the earliest and hopes to bring that film to Busan as well.


	The festival has kept inviting Kore-eda back since his debut, and the opening ceremony even featured a piece of music named after him. “It is a city and a film festival for which I have exceptionally strong feelings,” he said.

	He was joined by “Look Back” cast members Deguchi Natsuki, Makita Aju, Mori Nana and Ishikawa Ruka.

	Kore-eda stumbled on the manga in a bookshop rather than through its serial run. “When I read it, I felt a shock like an impact,” he said. “It explored why people write stories, or in my case, why one makes films – that sort of creative impulse, or the heavy burden or karma that artists carry.”

	On set, he avoided detailed scene-by-scene instruction and concentrated instead on the hours the four actors spent together and on how the town looked as the light and seasons shifted. “The cast understood that very well, and they appeared in front of the camera as individuals truly living inside that town,” he said.

	As soon as the adaptation was confirmed, Kore-eda pushed for 35mm across all four seasons, in line with his longstanding conviction that anything that can be shot on celluloid ought to be. “Because there is no mindset of ‘we can fix it later,’ it creates a healthy tension for the cast and crew,” he said. “When that collective tension gathers, I believe it generates a magnetic field in that shooting location.”
	

	The rotoscoped animation sequence late in the film stems from a single line. After a competition win, Fujino remarks that her dream was to see her manga animated, a comment that temporarily splits the two central characters. Kore-eda said the animation Fujino later makes stands in for a future the pair never got to share.

	“Rather than conventional cel animation, rotoscoping sits halfway between live-action and drawn animation,” he said. “Having the characters move within the background art drawn by Kyoko felt like the most suitable form of expression.”

	The film opens and closes on shots of Deguchi seen from behind. For the last of these, she said, Kore-eda instructed her, “Show Kyoko through your back.” After a long stretch shooting in Akita with her co-star, Deguchi found herself filming alone. “It felt like she was there, but not there… so with my heart feeling completely empty, I did that shot,” she said.

	Makita, who plays Kyoko, is at Busan for the first time. Mori said she had done the Venice red carpet too, though the mood in Korea struck her as different. “There was a huge crowd, so I was nervous, but seeing everyone wave their hands made it so much fun,” she said.

schema.headline: Eddie Redmayne’s Kore-eda Hirokazu Film Is Still Being Scripted, Director Says at Busan

title: Skeet Ulrich Says His ‘Scream’ Arc Couldn’t Be Completed After Melissa Barrera’s Firing: ‘There’s No Billy Loomis’ Without Her
description: Skeet Ulrich, who starred in 1996’s “Scream” as Billy Loomis and later reprised the role in both 2022’s “Scream” and 2023’s “Scream VI,” has opened
body:
Skeet Ulrich, who starred in 1996’s “Scream” as Billy Loomis and later reprised the role in both 2022’s “Scream” and 2023’s “Scream VI,” has opened up about not being able to complete what he calls his “three-film arc” after his co-star, Melissa Barrera, was fired from the franchise.

	Speaking with US Weekly, Ulrich explained that he doesn’t see himself returning to the franchise because “without Melissa Barrera and Sam Loomis, there’s no Billy Loomis.” (Barrera played Sam Carpenter, who was revealed to be Loomis’ daughter.) “He was in her head. They had their chance at it and didn’t quite get to complete the three-film arc that they talked to me about.”
	

	After starring in “Scream” and “Scream VI,” Barrera was ousted from the films by “Scream” franchise producer Spyglass due to social media posts criticizing Israel amid the war in Gaza in 2023. At the time, the company said it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.”


	After the firing, Barrera’s on-screen sister, Jenna Ortega, announced she wouldn’t return for 2026’s “Scream 7.” Neither Barrera nor Ulrich appeared in the recent film, which starred Matthew Lillard, Neve Campbell, Courteney Cox, Isabel May, Jasmin Savoy Brown, Mason Gooding and others.

	Last month, Lillard, who starred alongside Ulrich in the original film, admitted he felt “ashamed” for acting in “Scream 7” after Barrera was ousted.
	

	“I went back to do ‘Scream,’ and I got called out. And I’m like, ‘Oh, fuck. That’s brutal,’” he said during a 30th anniversary screening of the original “Scream.” “I feel bad about that. I feel ashamed about that. Because in that moment I was so excited to go back, I didn’t really think about Melissa and that journey. I didn’t say no. I’m embarrassed; that’s the truth… I blew that. I’m on the wrong side of history for that. I still like being in the movie [but] it may not have been the best idea.”

schema.headline: Skeet Ulrich Says His ‘Scream’ Arc Couldn’t Be Completed After Melissa Barrera’s Firing: ‘There’s No Billy Loomis’ Without Her

title: Josh Goldstine to Oversee Marketing and Distribution at Warner Bros., Paramount and All Skydance Film Labels (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Seasoned Hollywood marketer Josh Goldstine will be tapped for a massive new role at Skydance — encompassing Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures and all
body:
Seasoned Hollywood marketer Josh Goldstine will be tapped for a massive new role at Skydance — encompassing Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures and all subsequent film labels — sources told Variety.

	Goldstine will oversee marketing and distribution across all theatrical film. One knowledgeable insider said Goldstine met today with WB marketing execs Dana Nussbaum, Christian Davin and John Stanford — as well as Jeff Goldstein, president of global theatrical distribution. All four will report to Goldstine in the new structure.
	

	Reps for Warner Bros. Pictures and Paramount had no immediate comment on the matter.


	Goldstine joined Paramount in October 2025 as president of worldwide marketing and distribution, reporting to Paramount Pictures co-chairs Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg, following David Ellison’s acquisition of the company that August. Goldstine previously served as president of worldwide marketing at Warner Bros., departing in January 2025.

	The hiring is a remarkable comeback for Goldstine, who was abruptly dismissed in January 2025 by former WB motion picture chiefs Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy after four years with the studio. His exit came at the end of a turbulent 2024, which saw WB release flops like “Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga” and “Joker: Folie à Deux,” while at the same time fielding blockbuster hits like “Dune: Part Two,” “Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire” and “Beetlejuice Beetlejuice.”

	Ellison officially closed the deal for Warner Bros. on Tuesday, and the day prior he spelled out his leadership team for his new Hollywood powerhouse. After unveiling Ynon Kreiz, for Mattel chief, as his co-CEO, Ellison confirmed George Cheeks as co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance TV, Casey Bloys as co-chair and chief content officer and JB Perrette (previously Warner Bros. Discovery’s CEO and president of global streaming and games) as co-chair and chief business officer of both Skydance TV and Skydance DTC. Greenstein and Goldberg were named co-chairs of Skydance Motion Picture Group, overseeing both Warner Bros. and Paramount, and James Gunn and Peter Safran remain on board as co-chairs of DC Studios.

schema.headline: Josh Goldstine to Oversee Marketing and Distribution at Warner Bros., Paramount and All Skydance Film Labels (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Jack White Slams Trump as ‘Worst American of All Time’ Following Comment That Iran Can ‘Take Out’ L.A. and San Diego
description: Musician Jack White has fired back at Donald Trump following the president’s remarks made that Iran could “take out Los Angeles” and “San Diego” whi
body:
Musician Jack White has fired back at Donald Trump following the president’s remarks made that Iran could “take out Los Angeles” and “San Diego” while speaking about the international conflict on Monday at a rally in Nebraska.

	“Hey republicans and conservatives that live in L.A. and San Diego; how do you feel about your Fuhrer recommending that the cities you live in get attacked? Click the video I reposted and watch for yourself,” White shared on Instagram Tuesday. “Listen to the cult members CLAPPING and cheering for this. Let me take a wild guess: it was a joke, owning the libs, insert cult rhetoric here, etc. The allegiance these people have to this corrupt felon is so laughable and ignorant.”
	

	He continued: “That’s right, a U.S. ‘President’ that recommended that two major cities in our country be bombed because they don’t give total allegiance to his ego. Imagine any other President or elected official in history saying this. False flag incoming anyone? Just wait till next month when he begins enacting illegal measures to not allow democracy at the polls to prevail when the right lose badly in the mid term elections. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: The Worst American of All Time. #TWAAT”


	While onstage, Trump said that raising prices, due to the war, were a “small price to pay for keeping the world safe – keeping our country safe”. “They can take out a city,” Trump continued. “Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego.”

	White has long opposed Trump and has blasted the president many times before. In Aug. 2025, the “White Stripes” vocalist took to social media to call him a danger “not just to America but the entire world and that’s not an exaggeration,” and in Feb., mocked Trump’s appearance and track record of international conflict, writing, “Behold the leader of the ‘Board of Peace.’ For the next war announcement donny, may I suggest having your feet up on the Resolute desk while eating a Big Mac in a velvet track suit?”
	

	Gov. Gavin Newsom also spoke out after Trump’s comments, sharing several posts on X. “He is deranged and dangerous,” Newsom wrote in one post. “An American president is talking about Los Angeles and San Diego being ‘taken out.’ Where the hell is Congress? This is dangerous. The time to stand up is NOW,” he wrote in another.

	See White’s full post here.

schema.headline: Jack White Slams Trump as ‘Worst American of All Time’ Following Comment That Iran Can ‘Take Out’ L.A. and San Diego

title: Inside Omega’s James Bond Exhibition, From 007’s Toothbrush to His Passport and Mini Car Bombs
description: Omega marked Oct. 5, James Bond Day, by launching its new James Bond and Spectre watch collection and hosting a preview of the company’s 007 exhibit
body:
Omega marked Oct. 5, James Bond Day, by launching its new James Bond and Spectre watch collection and hosting a preview of the company’s 007 exhibition at its boutique at The Americana at Brand mall in Glendale on Monday night.

	The exhibition features props from various Bond movies, including the secret agent’s British passport from 2015’s “Spectre,” his toothbrush from “No Time to Die” (2021) and casino chips from “Casino Royale” (2006), among many other things.
	

	In a separate room, archival Omega James Bond watches were on display as were the new Bond and Spectre Seamaster Diver 300M pieces. There are six new watches. Three bear the James Bond symbol and the other three with the symbol of Spectre, 007’s enemy criminal syndicate headed by the white Persian cat-loving Ernst Stavro Blofeld.


	While the well-groomed guests — including actor Zane Phillips and a gaggle of models, influencers, creative directors, stylists and members of the press — oohed and aahed over the timepieces, the real main topic of conversation was the casting of the next James Bond.

	“Do you think they’ll announce the new James Bond tonight?” more than one guest was heard asking at the exhibition and during a dinner later on hosted by Omega CEO Raynald Aeschlimann at the Sunset Tower Hotel.

	“I hope they go with a newcomer,” was another frequent statement. Guests also debated why well-known actors like Jacob Elordi and Callum Turner were right, or not so right, for the part. “I was really hoping it would be Idris Elba,” one guest declared.
	

	More than a handful believe it will be Jack Lowden, especially after his “Slow Horses” co-star Gary Oldman made headlines in early September when he claimed in an interview that the next Bond had been picked. Oldman later clarified that he had no insight into the casting process and was just expressing hope that Lowden was going to get the job.

	Whoever gets the gig, one thing is for sure — he’ll be donning Omega watches. The company has been the official timepiece for the Bond franchise since 1995.

	Check out photos of the new Bond and Spectre watches below as well as items in the exhibition.

	The exhibition runs through Nov. 5.

schema.headline: Inside Omega’s James Bond Exhibition, From 007’s Toothbrush to His Passport and Mini Car Bombs

title: AMC+ Sets $3 Streaming Deal, Ahead of Buzzy 'Yaga' Premiere
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Streamer
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Streamer AMC+ has had a buzzy year, with shows like “The Vampire Lestat” and “The Audacity,” and franchises like “The Walking Dead” and “Doctor Who” all finding a home on the AMC Networks streaming service.

	Fans of “Heated Rivalry” will also want to tap into AMC+ to tune into “Yaga,” the Hudson Williams and Carrie Anne-Moss-starring mystery series that premieres on the streamer later this month on Oct. 23. 


	AMC+ normally costs $10.99/month for its premium plan or $109.99 annually, but a new deal gets you access to the streamer for just $39.99 for an entire year. That breaks down to just $3.33 a month and represents a 64% discount off the regular annual subscription price.


	You can claim the deal now on the AMC+ website or get it through Amazon Prime Video, which is showing the offer on its Prime Channels hub.

	The deal gets you access to the AMC+ Premium tier, which offers ad-free shows, movies and specials, the ability to download content for offline viewing, and unlimited streaming on up to five devices at one time. In addition to the AMC Networks library, your subscription also gets you access to TV shows and movies on BBC America, IFC, Sundance Now and horror streamer, Shudder.

	Everything is included in the $39.99 annual price — a one-time fee that saves you 64% off. This is the cheapest price we’ve seen for AMC+ since it launched in 2020.

	The offer is open to new subscribers and valid only until Oct. 12, so you’ll want to take advantage of the streaming deal while it’s still live, and have it on hand before “Yaga” premieres. Head to the Prime Channels hub here and navigate to the AMC+ section to claim the offer. 


	Note: there’s no promo code required, but you’ll need to be an Amazon Prime member to see the discounted pricing. Not a member? Get a 30-day free trial to Amazon Prime here and use it to claim the AMC+ streaming deal for October, in addition to all the other Prime member perks.

	The AMC+ streaming discount arrives on the heels of Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days, though it’s not necessarily tied to the October Prime Day event, which ends on Wednesday.

schema.headline: AMC+ Sets $3 Streaming Deal, Ahead of Buzzy 'Yaga' Premiere

            One of Patty Hearst's kidnappers, Bill Harris, has died.
      
    
            Harris passed away September 10 in San Francisco ... according to The New York Times.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Harris became infamous in 1974 as a top lieutenant of the Symbionese Liberation Army, a radical left wing group that kidnapped Patty from her Berkeley, CA apartment.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            While in captivity, Patty was forced to record a message denouncing her family and later appeared to embrace the SLA's ideology. She ultimately participated in the group's robbery of a San Francisco bank.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Patty was arrested in 1975 and later convicted of bank robbery. She was sentenced to seven years in prison but served about two years before President Jimmy Carter commuted what remained of her sentence.
      
    
            President Bill Clinton later granted Patty a full pardon in 2001.
      
    
            Bill was 81.

'Saved by the Bell' Dennis Haskins

            Dennis Haskins died from Parkinson's disease ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            TMZ obtained the "Saved by the Bell" actor's death certificate from the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, which lists Parkinson's disease as the immediate cause of death.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The certificate shows Dennis died September 27 at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank.
      

            The document also lists irritable bowel syndrome, depression, hypertension, and benign prostatic hyperplasia as other significant conditions.
      
    
            No one knew Dennis was battling Parkinson's before he died ... with his ex-wife, Sarah Quinones, telling us he had even cut off communication with close confidants to hide his diagnosis in recent years.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Dennis spent his final years in an assisted-living facility ... and he stopped returning calls and texts from Quinones and other close friends because he didn’t want anyone to know he was suffering from his illnesses.
      
    
            He starred as Principal Belding on "Saved by the Bell" and several of its spin-offs. He also racked up credits for "The Dukes of Hazzard," "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia," "The West Wing," "Victorious," and "A Million Ways to Die in the West."
      
    
            His agent Jay Schachter told us ... "It's a tragic loss. Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis, loved him even more. He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans."
